minutes.headline: TCP committee lost its quorum and adjourned without votes; it favored full asbestos and lead abatement and uniform windows.
minutes.summary: The design team briefed the committee on department meetings, civil/site scope questions, furniture, hazardous material abatement, and transaction windows. Committee members voiced consensus leanings on reusing furniture, limited sidewalk work, full abatement, and consistent solid transaction windows, but no formal votes were taken. A member's departure cost the meeting its quorum, so it adjourned and a working session was kept for Thursday.

what_happened.line: The TCP Building Design Committee lost its quorum when a member left, and adjourned without taking any votes.
Members leaned toward abating asbestos and lead paint in occupied spaces now, rather than later, though no vote was taken.
Members favored uniform, solid transaction windows, and the design team was asked for life-cycle cost comparisons of floors and other wear surfaces.
The committee expects to ask Town Meeting for one project number covering hard and soft costs, with alternates sorted out later in design.
The design team will ask Meridian about survey findings and a separate parcel, and the committee kept a Thursday working session.

why_it_matters: The single project number and the choice to abate hazardous materials now shape the cost residents will be asked to approve at Town Meeting, and that cost is paid mostly through taxes.
With no votes taken and quorum lost, the scope, finishes and furniture choices remain unsettled, so the eventual funding request could still change.
